title: What That Hand Paid
description:
Two months since you went in on the stolen tip from the café.
Today you opened the portfolio.

choices.text: It made money. But it feels wrong.
choices.result_text:
You made money.
But you knew how you made it.
Whatever you do with this money — where it came from doesn't change.

choices.text: It lost. And someone found out.
choices.result_text:
The stolen information was wrong anyway.
Then a message from someone who'd been at that table.
'You overheard us that day, didn't you?'
Two things lost at once.

title: The Information You Didn't Use
description:
You overheard the tip at the café — and ultimately walked away without using it.
Today that ticker made the news.
[OO Stock Up 3.4x in Six Months]

choices.text: Disappointing — but it was the right call.
choices.result_text:
3.4x.
The number stayed in front of your eyes for a while.
But so did how you would have made that money.
It was the right call.
Even if it hurt.

choices.text: Should've just put it in.
choices.result_text:
3.4x.
Keeping this in mind leads you to do it again next time.
The pain of opportunity cost is the most common way people rationalize bad decisions.

title: A Chance to Make It Right
description:
You'd made money from the stolen café tip.
It never sat right with you.
Today the person appeared.
You could look away and pass.

choices.text: Come clean
choices.result_text:
'That day at the café — I'm sorry.'
The other person paused. '...I already knew. Just be more careful.'
Something heavy lifted.
Redemption starts with words.

choices.text: Let it pass again
choices.result_text:
You passed again.
The chance came and you missed it again.
If the same situation comes up next time — you'll probably pass again.

title: The End of Waiting
description:
A year ago you chose to act honestly at the café and wait.
Today the investment you'd quietly marked in your mind made an official announcement.

choices.text: Enter based on the official disclosure
choices.result_text:
Waiting hadn't been waiting for the information — it was waiting for the right method.
You made money.
Same result, but this time you could hold your head up.

choices.text: Too late. Already up too much.
choices.result_text:
It was already up 30% by the time you checked.
You watched without greed.
Waiting doesn't always return profit.
But the method was right.

title: What You Lost Honestly
description:
You went in honestly at the café — and lost.
Today a similar investment opportunity showed up.
The memory came first.

choices.text: Look more carefully this time before entering
choices.result_text:
A week of analysis.
The loss became the benchmark for this analysis.
If the lost money was tuition — this judgment was the product of it.

choices.text: Skip this one. Haven't recovered yet.
choices.result_text:
You sat it out.
Not overextending is also investing.
When you're ready — back in.

title: The Limits of Being Clever
description:
You thought you were being smart at the café — and still lost.
Six months later you went back and reviewed the trade.
Now you could see where it went wrong.

choices.text: Write up the review in notes
choices.result_text:
Three mistakes visible.
Including: 'feeling smart' is the most dangerous moment.
Those notes became the standard for the next trade.

choices.text: Conclude it was just bad luck.
choices.result_text:
You called it luck.
But without a review, the same mistake repeats.
'Luck' isn't a conclusion — it's avoidance.

title: Someone from That Café
description:
You overheard investment talk at the café and did nothing with it.
Today on the street you ran into one of the two people from that conversation.
You were close enough to recognize each other.

choices.text: Pass without a word
choices.result_text:
You passed.
They didn't seem to notice.
The judgment from that day felt vindicated.
Not using what you overheard.

choices.text: Speak first
choices.result_text:
You spoke.
They asked where they'd seen you.
'That café. Briefly.'
A short exchange.
Where it leads — unknown. But something started.

title: Humility's Expiration Date
description:
After what happened at the café, you were humble for a while.
Six months passed.
Today another strong-sounding tip came in.
Same feeling as back then.

choices.text: Verify it first, like last time
choices.result_text:
You checked first.
This one was fake.
Humility had become a skill.
Not forgetting what you learned — that's how one experience lasts a long time.

choices.text: This time is different. Go straight in.
choices.result_text:
You went straight in.
Wrong.
The humility learned at the café was tested again six months later.
And failed again.

title: That Day's Account
description:
The day you kept betting to win back what you'd lost.
Home. You tallied the account.
Total loss: 1.4x your monthly rent.

choices.text: Delete the betting app
choices.result_text:
Deleted.
Chasing losses — the longer you wait to stop, the more expensive it gets.
Today was the cheapest day it could be.

choices.text: Go back next weekend and recover it
choices.result_text:
You went back.
Lost more.
Chasing a loss always ends in a bigger loss.

title: Two Months Away from the Track
description:
Two months since you decided to step back.
Today a friend said they were heading to the track, asked if you wanted to come.
No particular reason — just for fun.

choices.text: Pass. No explanation needed.
choices.result_text:
'I'll skip.'
Friend asked 'Why?'
'Just.'
Two months held.

choices.text: It's just watching — go along
choices.result_text:
You went.
Meant to just watch — tried one.
The pause broke.
Two months gone in one moment.

title: The Value of Analysis
description:
At the track you'd built a habit of reading races.
Today looking at a stock chart — that same approach came back.
The pattern-reading method was similar.

choices.text: Apply it to analyze a stock
choices.result_text:
Half right, half wrong.
Still better than entering with no framework.
Wherever you learned it — an analysis habit becomes a skill.

choices.text: Tracks are tracks and stocks are stocks.
choices.result_text:
Blindly applying lessons from one domain is dangerous.
Apply with reasons, not instinct.
That judgment itself — was already analysis.

title: That Tip's Record
description:
Three months since you asked someone who looked like an expert at the track.
Since then, three bets.
1 win, 2 losses.

choices.text: Stop relying on other people's tips
choices.result_text:
33% hit rate.
They didn't know either.
Someone who looks like they know and someone who actually knows — different.
The judgment has to be yours.

choices.text: Find better tipsters
choices.result_text:
You paid for premium picks.
Wrong.
Nobody sells real certainty at a racetrack.
If they were certain, they'd use it themselves — not sell it.

title: That Contact
description:
The restaurant owner who said 'My son's company has an opening' — you still had the number.
Current situation was tighter than when she'd offered.

choices.text: Reach out
choices.result_text:
The son answered.
'My mother mentioned you. Want to come in?'
A lead from a side-dish restaurant owner.
Paths open from the most unexpected places.

choices.text: Not the right time yet
choices.result_text:
Decided it wasn't time yet.
Kept the number saved.
A small kindness became a small possibility. Unclear when it'll be used.

title: The Person You Warned
description:
Half a year ago you warned someone who was about to get scammed.
Today a message from that person.
"I'm so grateful for what you said back then."

choices.text: "I'm glad. Hope things are going well."
choices.result_text:
'If you're nearby, I'd love to buy you a meal.'
A word to a stranger — came back like this six months later.
Good things are remembered.

choices.text: "It was nothing."
choices.result_text:
'It was nothing.'
They said 'It was everything to me.'
The person it happened to knows its value best.

title: Subsidy Result
description:
Four months since you applied for youth housing support.
Today a text arrived.
[Youth Housing Support Review Result]

choices.text: Approved
choices.result_text:
200,000 won/month, 12 months.
2.4 million won total.
Money that wouldn't exist if you hadn't applied.
Knowing what's out there and using it — that's also a skill.

choices.text: Declined
choices.result_text:
Declined.
Income slightly over the threshold.
Disappointing — but you have to apply to find out.
Went back and looked for other support programs.

title: What Becoming a Regular Means
description:
It's been a while since you got to know the celebrity who frequents that café.
Today you ran into them again.
This time they nodded first.

choices.text: Exchange a casual greeting
choices.result_text:
'Hello.'
They said 'You're here a lot.'
Networks in Gangnam — built from small recognitions like this too.
Something you can't force.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice. Don't want to make it awkward.
choices.result_text:
You looked away.
They'd started to say something — sat down instead.
There are many ways to navigate Gangnam.
This is one of them.
